If the points with position vectors \(6 \hat{i}+11 \hat{j}+11 \hat{k}\), \(\frac{9}{2} \hat{i}+\beta \hat{j}-8 \hat{k}, \alpha \hat{i}+10 \hat{j}+13 \hat{k}\) are collinear, then \((19 \alpha-6 \beta)^2\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 8 Apr (Shift 1)]
questions.explanation:
Let \(A(6,11,11), B\left(\frac{9}{2}, \beta,-8\right), C(\alpha, 10,13) \)

Collinearity \(\Rightarrow \overrightarrow{A B}\) and \(\overrightarrow{A C}\) are parallel:

\(\overrightarrow{A B}=\left(\frac{9}{2}-6, \beta-11,-8-11\right)=\left(-\frac{3}{2}, \beta-11,-19\right)\)
\(\overrightarrow{A C}=(\alpha-6,-1,2)\)

Hence the component ratios are equal:

\(\frac{-\frac{3}{2}}{\alpha-6}=\frac{\beta-11}{-1}=\frac{-19}{2}\)

From the first equality:

\(\alpha-6=\frac{-\frac{3}{2}}{-\frac{19}{2}}=\frac{3}{19} \Rightarrow \alpha=6+\frac{3}{19}=\frac{117}{19}\)

From the second equality:

\(\beta-11=\frac{19}{2} \Rightarrow \beta=11+\frac{19}{2}=\frac{41}{2}\)

Now \(19 \alpha-6 \beta=19 \cdot \frac{117}{19}-6 \cdot \frac{41}{2}=117-123=-6\)

and so \((19 \alpha-6 \beta)^2=(-6)^2=36\)
